Chapter 1 D-DAY

An ordinary morning ends before anyone understands what has truly begun.

Mick Braddock tries to keep Mei and their four children alive as the city collapses around them. At a military installation, Major James Hanson finds reports of attacks multiplying far too quickly. At the Pentagon, Colonel Samuel Salazar realizes that distant incidents are part of the same crisis.

Work in progress

This page contains only canonical passages that have already been written. All three perspectives have been received, but the continuations of Mick’s, Hanson’s, and Samuel’s accounts are still in development.

BRADDOCK FILE // PASSAGE 01

Mick Braddock

First person // family testimony

06:00 → 07:40AVAILABLE

The morning begins with a run, teasing between siblings, and a family breakfast. When the news announces martial law, none of them imagines that the reason is already on its way.

EXCERPT A // AFTER 07:00

It was already past seven when we gathered around the kitchen table. While the children ate, I listened to the news on television. In one of the reports, we heard that the government had declared martial law. I just didn’t hear why.

“Dad, what is martial law?” asked Elisa, the youngest.

“Well, sweetheart, martial law is like the rules Mommy and Daddy make here at home about what you can and cannot do.”

“Yeah, unless you’re Maya, who doesn’t like those rules very much and is always trying to break them,” Chris teased, laughing.

“Shut up, you idiot!” Maya snapped, kicking him under the table.

“Hey, hey, hey! No fighting. Eat so we can get going,” Mei warned them.

07:40 // TRAFFIC AT A STANDSTILL
EXCERPT B // FIVE HELICOPTERS

During the traffic jam, the first helicopter passed overhead. About five minutes later, a second crossed the sky in the same direction. Before ten minutes had passed, three more followed the same route.

We spent a few more minutes together as a family, until a motorcycle came racing past and tore off the car’s side mirror, startling all of us.

“My God...” Mei said, shaken.

After the shock, she made an interesting observation:

“That’s the fifth helicopter to pass over us. What do you think is happening?”

PASSAGE INTERRUPTED

The next record begins after normality can no longer be recovered.

HANSON FILE // PASSAGE 01

Major James Hanson

Third person // military response

05:00 → 06:40PARTIAL

Hanson returns from a mission and is summoned by General Anderson. Inside the control center, incidents being treated as ordinary violence begin to form a pattern.

EXCERPT A // CONTROL CENTER

Hanson and Anderson left the room and headed directly to the control center. The place was usually calm and quiet, but for some reason there was a great commotion among the soldiers.

“What’s happening, General? The men seem a little... unsettled.”

“That’s what I want to show you, Major. Look.”

Anderson brought up a series of reports on the screen. Several people claimed they were being attacked by other people.

“These reports keep increasing. We suspect some new outbreak of rabies.”

Hanson examined the report and reviewed the recorded messages.

“Is all of this from today, General?”

“The reports in your hands and on the screen... Yes. They’re happening now.”

INTERCEPTED AUDIO // TIME UNCONFIRMED
EXCERPT B // DD-RADIO-TAYLOR

The general played audio intercepted from one of the officers’ radios:

“We need backup! I repeat: we need backup here on Taylor Avenue! Something is wrong. People are attacking people and... Hey, don’t come any closer! I’ll shoot... I said... Hey... N-no... Aaah!”

The recording ended with gunshots in the background.

Security footage showed three people advancing on the officer even after they had been shot.

“General, I’ve seen many things in this career, and this... This goes beyond anything I’ve ever seen. They were shot at point-blank range and they didn’t go down...”

“We need to issue a red alert and try to contain this before it spreads.”

06:40 // DEPLOYMENT ORDER

Hanson receives the list of incidents and deploys the soldiers. The continuation of this perspective is still being written.

SALAZAR FILE // PASSAGE 01

Samuel Jordan Salazar

Third person // strategic response

04:30 → 07:10PARTIAL

At the Pentagon, Samuel tracks incidents reported across different parts of the country. What appeared to be isolated violence begins to form a simultaneous pattern—and he is the first to treat the phenomenon as a national crisis.

EXCERPT A // FIRST REPORTS

At 04:30, Colonel Samuel Salazar, a senior Strategic Planning officer at the Department of Defense, was investigating a series of incidents reported across the country. Until then, every report had ended with the same theory: an outbreak caused by drugs or powerful substances.

A staff member called him over to a workstation surrounded by monitors.

“What happened?”

The screens showed people attacking other people in several places at the same time. The first incidents came from smaller communities and, at first, local police appeared to be containing the threat. Samuel, however, remembered similar cases and went on alert.

“Keep me informed if more cases like these appear.”

By nearly five in the morning, civilian reports were growing too quickly to be dismissed as coincidence. Samuel returned to his office and, at exactly 05:00, issued a red alert to the Armed Forces: proceed with caution, contain the incidents, and keep the situation under control until further orders.

06:30 // BRIEFING ROOM
EXCERPT B // MAXIMUM ALERT

At 06:30, Samuel was called to the briefing room, where Armed Forces officers and government officials were waiting for an update.

“The situation has not improved; it has only grown worse. Reports of people attacking other people keep rising. We can confirm this is an outbreak. We still do not know what kind, but we do know that those who are bitten or wounded are turning into the same thing that attacked them.”

When questioned about the bites, Samuel explained that the recordings showed attackers tearing chunks from their victims. Hospitals crowded with the wounded were also beginning to report attacks inside their own wards.

“The truth, ladies and gentlemen, is that we are now at maximum alert.”

When the Vice President asked what should be done, Samuel recommended the immediate declaration of martial law. People were to remain inside, lock every door and window, and allow no one in—not friends, not relatives—while the government attempted to contain the outbreak.

“Washington is among the worst-hit areas right now. Get the President out of the White House immediately, sir.”

After several moments of silence, the Vice President authorized the plan and ordered the President’s evacuation. The meeting ended, and Samuel asked his assistant Bethany to try to reach Elena, his wife, and to take her own family to the UN ferry as well.

Samuel ordered the building evacuated immediately. When he boarded the helicopter at 07:10, a soldier reported that the Armed Forces base had fallen after infected troops returned and spread the infection throughout the compound. There was no confirmation that General Anderson had survived.

Before departure, Samuel tried once more to call Elena, who was traveling through Spain with their children. None of them answered.

07:10 // RECORD INTERRUPTED

The available transcript ends during the Pentagon evacuation. The continuation of this perspective is still being written.

NAVY // HANSON MEMORYMark Connor — a service memoryThe record does not indicate a chain of command.
